evidence_chain: Fact: SPS's 2025 Form 10-K reported 2025 revenue of $751.5 million, versus $637.8 million in 2024 and $536.9 million in 2023. Source: SEC 2025 Form 10-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001092699/000109269926000012/spsc-20251231.htm

Fact: SPS's 2025 Form 10-K reported recurring revenue from recurring revenue customers equal to 96% of total revenue in 2025, compared with 94% in 2024 and 2023. Source: SEC 2025 Form 10-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001092699/000109269926000012/spsc-20251231.htm

Fact: SPS's 2025 Form 10-K stated that no customer represented 1% or more of total revenue for 2025, 2024, or 2023. Source: SEC 2025 Form 10-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001092699/000109269926000012/spsc-20251231.htm

Fact: SPS's 2025 Form 10-K describes the company as operating a global supply-chain network where companies connect once and can transact with thousands of trading partners across channels. Source: SEC 2025 Form 10-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001092699/000109269926000012/spsc-20251231.htm

Fact: SPS reported Q1 2026 revenue of $192.1 million, up 6% year over year from $181.5 million, and recurring revenue growth of 7%. Source: SPS Commerce Q1 2026 release filed with SEC, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1092699/000109269926000042/er_q126.htm

Fact: SPS's Q1 2026 release guided full-year 2026 revenue to $796.0 million to $802.0 million, representing 6% to 7% growth over 2025. Source: SPS Commerce Q1 2026 release filed with SEC, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1092699/000109269926000042/er_q126.htm

Inference: The combination of high recurring revenue mix, low customer concentration, and a many-to-many trading-partner network is consistent with a networked operating-infrastructure business rather than a single-customer or single-retailer software tool.
Hypothesis: The 2026 growth slowdown may be cyclical or segment-specific rather than structural if retention, customer additions, ARPU, organic growth, and transaction volumes remain resilient.
Hypothesis: SPS's true moat may be in accumulated retailer-specific compliance logic, onboarding know-how, transaction templates, and partner graph density, not only in software functionality.
falsification_plan: Downgrade if recurring revenue mix falls materially for multiple quarters or if non-recurring/acquisition-driven revenue becomes a larger share of growth.
Downgrade if gross retention or net revenue retention weakens for several quarters, especially among core fulfillment/connectivity customers.
Downgrade if customer count, ARPU, organic revenue growth, and transaction volumes all decelerate at the same time, indicating saturation rather than temporary budget caution.
Downgrade if management disclosures show reported growth is driven mainly by acquisitions while core fulfillment/network revenue is flat or declining.
Downgrade if major retailers, marketplaces, or ERP vendors shift supplier connectivity to in-house portals, open APIs, or competing networks in a way that reduces SPS switching costs.
Downgrade if retailer mandate evidence weakens, partner additions slow, implementation backlog shrinks, or suppliers increasingly cite SPS as optional rather than operationally necessary.
Downgrade if chargeback avoidance, ASN/invoice accuracy, onboarding speed, or compliance-management benefits are not supported by customer case studies, product documentation, or call commentary.
deep_reports.hidden_signal_to_verify: The hidden signal is whether SPS's trading-partner graph is still compounding even as reported growth slows. Upgrade evidence would include stable or rising recurring revenue mix, strong gross retention, healthy net revenue retention, customer additions, ARPU expansion, organic growth excluding acquisitions, rising fulfillment/network transaction activity, new retailer mandates or partner additions, and evidence that suppliers continue to outsource EDI/compliance work rather than shifting to retailer portals, in-house integrations, APIs, or competing networks.
next_research_tasks: Pull SPS's latest 10-Q and earnings-call transcript to extract customer count, ARPU, retention metrics, fulfillment growth, and management commentary on supplier budget pressure.
Separate organic growth from acquired growth, especially any contribution from Carbon6 or other purchased assets, and compare organic recurring revenue growth with reported recurring revenue growth.

Build a quarterly KPI table: total revenue growth, recurring revenue growth, recurring revenue percentage, adjusted EBITDA margin, customer count, ARPU, net revenue retention if disclosed, gross retention if disclosed, and buyback activity.

Search SPS product documentation and customer case studies for concrete evidence of retailer-specific EDI maps, ASN/invoice/order workflows, chargeback reduction, onboarding time savings, and compliance automation.
Check major retailer supplier requirements and vendor manuals for EDI/ASN/invoice mandates that could create durable third-party demand for platforms like SPS.
Compare SPS against alternative supplier-connectivity routes: retailer portals, ERP-native integrations, middleware/API platforms, EDI VANs, logistics platforms, and marketplace-native tools.
Review whether the Amazon 3P-related headwind is temporary, segment-specific, or a sign that marketplace platform owners can change economics in ways that reduce SPS's take rate.

Interview or collect channel checks from small and mid-sized brands selling into Walmart, Target, Costco, Amazon, grocery, specialty retail, and wholesale distributors to verify whether SPS is treated as a must-have operating layer or a replaceable vendor.

Monitor 2026 and 2027 quarters for the decisive pattern: healthy retention plus slower new spend would support a temporary-slowdown thesis; simultaneous deterioration in retention, ARPU, customer additions, and organic growth would falsify the chokepoint thesis.
risks: Growth deceleration risk: Q1 2026 revenue growth of 6% and full-year guidance of 6% to 7% growth are materially slower than the 2023-2025 revenue CAGR implied by reported annual revenue figures.
Saturation risk: If most reachable suppliers already have modern EDI/connectivity solutions, incremental customer additions and ARPU expansion may decline.
Organic-growth opacity risk: Acquisitions can obscure whether the core retail supplier network is still compounding organically.
Platform displacement risk: Large retailers, marketplaces, ERPs, logistics platforms, or API-based integration vendors could reduce the need for third-party EDI networks.
Supplier-budget risk: Smaller suppliers may defer software spend when consumer demand weakens, retail inventories normalize, or marketplace economics deteriorate.

Mandate concentration risk without revenue concentration: Even if no single customer represents more than 1% of revenue, a small number of large retailer mandates may influence many supplier purchasing decisions.
Pricing and churn risk: Price increases, platform fees, or product packaging changes may improve ARPU but cause churn among smaller or lower-volume suppliers.
Narrative risk: The stock may be valued as a high-quality recurring-revenue software compounder; if growth stays mid-single-digit, valuation support could weaken even if the business remains durable.
deep_reports.supply_chain_position: Consumer retail operating infrastructure layer. Downstream demand comes from retailers, marketplaces, wholesale channels, ecommerce, DTC, and omnichannel fulfillment. Immediate users include brands, suppliers, distributors, manufacturers, and logistics providers. SPS sits between these parties as a transaction-connectivity and compliance-workflow layer: EDI maps, order documents, ASNs, invoices, product data synchronization, partner onboarding, retailer-specific document requirements, and exception handling. It is one or two steps away from visible consumer demand, which makes the signal less obvious than retailers, brands, marketplaces, or ecommerce platforms.
deep_reports.thesis_cn: 核心假设：SPS Commerce 可能是消费零售供应链中的运营基础设施瓶颈。品牌商、供应商、分销商、制造商和物流服务商在对接零售商、批发、电商、Marketplace 和 DTC 渠道时，需要处理 EDI 映射、订单、ASN、发票、商品数据、交易伙伴接入、零售商特定合规规则和异常处理。SPS 的价值不只是“软件订阅”，而是把大量分散、重复、容易出错的零售交易连接工作外包给一个已有交易伙伴网络的平台。事实层面，SPS 2025 年 Form 10-K 披露其 2025 年收入为 7.515 亿美元，经常性收入占总收入 96%，最大客户占比低于 1%，并称其网络让公司一次连接即可与数千个交易伙伴交易。2026 年一季度收入同比增长 6%，经常性收入同比增长 7%。推论层面，如果客户留存、ARPU、客户新增、交易伙伴网络深度和有机增长仍然健康，那么 2026 年增速放缓可能更多是供应商 IT 支出、Amazon 3P 或短期预算压力造成，而不一定说明网络效应失效。反过来，如果新增客户、ARPU、留存、有机增长和交易量同步走弱，则应把该 thesis 降级为成熟软件资产，而不是供应链瓶颈资产。
deep_reports.thesis_en: Core hypothesis: SPS Commerce may be an operating-infrastructure chokepoint in consumer retail supply chains. Brands, suppliers, distributors, manufacturers, and logistics providers that sell through retailers, wholesale channels, ecommerce, marketplaces, and DTC channels must maintain EDI maps, purchase orders, ASNs, invoices, product data, trading-partner onboarding, retailer-specific compliance logic, and exception handling. SPS is therefore not merely a generic SaaS vendor; the possible moat is the outsourcing of fragmented, recurring, error-prone retail transaction connectivity into a scaled trading-partner network. As factual support, SPS's 2025 Form 10-K reports 2025 revenue of $751.5 million, recurring revenue equal to 96% of total revenue, no customer above 1% of revenue, and describes a global supply-chain network where companies connect once and can transact with thousands of trading partners. SPS's Q1 2026 release reported revenue growth of 6% and recurring revenue growth of 7% year over year. The key inference is that if retention, ARPU, customer additions, trading-partner depth, and organic growth remain healthy, the 2026 slowdown may reflect supplier IT-budget delays, Amazon 3P pressure, or temporary spending caution rather than loss of network effects. If customer additions, ARPU, retention, organic growth, and transaction volumes all deteriorate together, the thesis should be downgraded from chokepoint infrastructure to mature application software.
deep_reports.title_cn: SPS Commerce：消费零售供应链里的 EDI / 合规连接收费站
deep_reports.title_en: SPS Commerce: A Retail-Supply-Chain EDI and Compliance Connectivity Tollbooth
deep_reports.why_underfollowed: SPSC can screen as generic application software, while the hidden signal sits inside mundane but mission-critical retail operations: retailer-specific EDI maps, supplier onboarding, compliance rules, ASN and invoice accuracy, chargeback avoidance, partner-network density, and labor saved in maintaining many bilateral connections. These workflows are not usually visible in consumer-brand sales data, retail comps, or ecommerce GMV headlines. The market may therefore focus on headline SaaS growth deceleration while missing whether the platform still has a durable network-effect role in retail supplier connectivity.

evidence_chain: Fact: Descartes reported FY2026 services revenue of $677.2 million, representing 93% of total revenues; professional services and other revenues were $49.3 million and license revenues were $2.5 million. Source: https://www.descartes.com/resources/news/descartes-announces-fiscal-2026-fourth-quarter-and-annual-financial-results

Fact: The FY2026 annual filing states services revenues were $677.2 million in FY2026, $590.2 million in FY2025, and $520.9 million in FY2024, representing 93%, 91%, and 91% of total revenues respectively. Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001050140/000110465926026450/dsgx-20260131xex99d2.htm

Fact: Descartes' FY2026 filing says 2026 revenue growth from new and existing customers was driven by global trade intelligence, routing, and transportation management solutions; it also says 2025 acquisitions contributed an incremental $27.1 million in revenues in FY2026. Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001050140/000110465926026450/dsgx-20260131xex99d2.htm

Fact: Descartes reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $193.6 million and services revenue of $180.5 million, with a five-quarter table showing services revenue of $156.6 million in Q1 FY2026, $166.8 million in Q2 FY2026, $173.7 million in Q3 FY2026, $180.1 million in Q4 FY2026, and $180.5 million in Q1 FY2027. Source: https://www.descartes.com/resources/news/descartes-announces-fiscal-2027-first-quarter-financial-results

Fact: Q1 FY2027 gross margin was 78%, net income as a percentage of revenues was 25%, and adjusted EBITDA margin was 46%, based on Descartes' Q1 FY2027 release. Source: https://www.descartes.com/resources/news/descartes-announces-fiscal-2027-first-quarter-financial-results
Fact: Current market data on June 9, 2026 showed DSGX market capitalization of approximately $6.47 billion. Source: web finance quote for DSGX, latest trade time Tuesday, June 09, 2026 13:49:12 UTC.

Inference: The high services revenue mix, recurring revenue profile, and logistics-network framing support the broad logistics infrastructure thesis. However, they do not by themselves prove that consumer retail/ecommerce is the dominant value driver.

Hypothesis: If ecommerce, retail replenishment, cross-border compliance, and carrier connectivity are materially represented in revenue and organic growth, Descartes may be a consumer supply-chain chokepoint hidden inside a logistics-software classification.
falsification_plan: Falsify if retail, ecommerce, CPG, parcel, or consumer-linked logistics exposure is immaterial relative to broader trade compliance, routing, freight forwarding, or generic transportation management modules.
Falsify if FY2027 and FY2028 filings show growth primarily from acquisitions while organic services growth from new and existing customers decelerates materially.
Falsify if customer references and case studies are mostly non-consumer industrial, government, freight-forwarding, or generic compliance accounts without meaningful retail/ecommerce workflows.
Falsify if retention, attach-rate, connected-party, transaction-volume, or network-participation metrics are absent or deteriorating where disclosed.
Falsify if customers can replace Descartes modules with internal systems or competing point solutions without meaningful switching cost, compliance risk, or network-disruption cost.
Falsify if tariff/customs complexity rises but Descartes does not show corresponding demand, commentary, services revenue resilience, or module attach benefits.
deep_reports.hidden_signal_to_verify: The key hidden signal is whether Descartes has a durable network effect around consumer-linked shipment, customs, carrier, ecommerce, and B2B messages. The upgrade evidence would be explicit disclosure or customer proof showing that retail/ecommerce/CPG/logistics-provider customers represent a material share of revenue or organic growth; that customer workflows depend on Descartes' connected-party network rather than replaceable point tools; and that trade/tariff/customs complexity increases usage, retention, or module attach rates.
next_research_tasks: Pull the full FY2026 annual report and Q1 FY2027 shareholder report; extract exact wording on global trade intelligence, transportation management, routing, ecommerce, customs/regulatory compliance, B2B connectivity, and acquisitions.
Build a module map with columns for product, target customer, consumer relevance, switching cost, evidence strength, and whether revenue is organic or acquired.
Search investor presentations and conference transcripts for customer counts, connected-party counts, shipment/message transaction metrics, retention, net revenue retention, and vertical exposure.

Identify customer references in retail, ecommerce marketplaces, CPG, apparel, footwear, parcel delivery, 3PL, customs brokerage, and cross-border merchants; separate named customers from marketing language.

Quantify acquisition contribution since FY2025, including OCR, ASD, BoxTop, Assure Assist/MyCarrierPortal, Sellercloud, PackageRoute, Finale, and any FY2027 acquisitions; separate organic growth from acquired revenue where possible.

Compare Descartes against reference leaders and substitutes such as carrier platforms, ERP/TMS suites, ecommerce shipping tools, customs brokers' internal systems, and EDI/B2B networks to assess replaceability.
Track policy catalysts: tariff changes, sanctions screening, customs modernization, de minimis rule changes, cross-border ecommerce rules, and retailer supply-chain compliance requirements.

Create an upgrade checklist: material retail/ecommerce vertical disclosure, evidence of network transaction growth, rising services revenue without acquisition dependence, named customer proof, high retention/attach metrics, and management commentary linking trade complexity to demand.
risks: Segmentation risk: the company may be more exposed to general logistics, freight forwarding, trade compliance, and enterprise transportation management than to consumer retail or ecommerce specifically.
Acquisition-dependence risk: FY2026 growth included contribution from acquisitions; if organic growth from new and existing customers weakens, the network thesis should be downgraded.
Replaceability risk: customers may treat individual modules as point solutions rather than as hard-to-replace network infrastructure.
Freight-cycle and retail-volume risk: if revenue is more transaction-volume-sensitive than subscription-like, retail freight downturns could pressure growth.

Regulatory complexity cuts both ways: tariffs, sanctions, customs, de minimis, and cross-border rules can increase demand for compliance software, but abrupt policy changes or trade slowdowns can also reduce shipment activity.

Valuation/expectations risk: this report does not make a buy/sell call; a mid-cap SaaS/logistics infrastructure company can be operationally strong while still having market expectations that already price in durable growth.
Disclosure risk: management may not disclose enough vertical, module, or network-transaction detail to prove the consumer chokepoint thesis.
deep_reports.supply_chain_position: Consumer demand layer -> retail/ecommerce order flow -> fulfillment and inventory movement -> parcel/LTL/FTL/ocean/air shipment execution -> carrier and logistics-provider connectivity -> customs, tariff, sanctions and regulatory compliance -> B2B/EDI/network messages -> Descartes Global Logistics Network, transportation management, routing, ecommerce shipping/fulfillment, customs/regulatory compliance, global trade intelligence, and B2B connectivity modules. Reference leaders in the visible lane are retailers, marketplaces, brands, parcel carriers, freight brokers, and 3PLs; Descartes sits one or two steps upstream as the software/message/compliance coordination layer.
deep_reports.thesis_cn: 假设：Descartes 可能是消费供应链的二阶卡点，而不是传统意义上的零售软件公司。它的核心价值不在直接触达消费者，而在连接零售商、电商卖家、物流服务商、承运商、关务代理、海关/监管节点和运输管理系统所需的数据、合规和消息流。事实：公司 FY2026 服务收入为 6.772 亿美元，占总收入 93%；FY2027 Q1 服务收入为 1.805 亿美元，连续五个季度服务收入从 FY2026 Q1 的 1.566 亿美元增长到 FY2027 Q1 的 1.805 亿美元。推论：高服务收入占比和连续服务收入增长支持其具备经常性网络软件属性。仍待验证：这些服务收入中有多少来自零售、电商履约、跨境包裹、供应商 EDI/B2B 消息、承运商连接和消费品供应链，而不是更宽泛的贸易合规、货代、路由、运输管理或并购整合模块。
deep_reports.thesis_en: Hypothesis: Descartes may be a second-order chokepoint in consumer supply chains rather than a direct retail software vendor. Its potential importance comes from the data, compliance, and message flows that connect retailers, ecommerce sellers, logistics service providers, carriers, customs brokers, government/regulatory nodes, and transportation management systems. Fact: FY2026 services revenue was $677.2 million, representing 93% of total revenue; Q1 FY2027 services revenue was $180.5 million, with services revenue increasing across the five-quarter table from $156.6 million in Q1 FY2026 to $180.5 million in Q1 FY2027. Inference: the high services mix and sequential service revenue growth support a recurring network-software profile. Unverified: how much of that revenue is tied specifically to retail, ecommerce fulfillment, cross-border parcels, supplier EDI/B2B messaging, carrier connectivity, and consumer-goods supply chains versus broader trade compliance, freight forwarding, routing, transportation management, or acquisition-led modules.
deep_reports.title_cn: Descartes：消费供应链背后的物流、关务与网络消息基础设施
deep_reports.title_en: Descartes: Logistics, Customs, and Network-Messaging Infrastructure Behind Consumer Supply Chains
deep_reports.why_underfollowed: Descartes is usually categorized as logistics software, transportation management, global trade intelligence, or supply-chain SaaS, so consumer investors may miss the hidden exposure. The consumer signal is buried inside operational message traffic: retail replenishment, ecommerce shipment creation, cross-border checkout/clearance, carrier-rate selection, denied-party screening, customs filings, and supplier-to-retailer B2B integration. Because the company is not branded as a consumer platform and does not appear to sell consumer products, the market may under-map it to retail/ecommerce resilience, tariff complexity, de minimis/customs rule changes, and omnichannel fulfillment complexity.

evidence_chain: [Fact from provided brief / 2025 Form 10-K summary] Manhattan's named core investment/product directions include Unified Omnichannel Commerce and Digital Supply Chain.
[Fact from provided brief / 2025 Form 10-K summary] 2025 cloud subscription revenue was $408.1M, up 21% year over year, and represented about 38% of total revenue.
[Fact from provided brief / 2025 Form 10-K summary] RPO was about $2.2B, up 25%, and more than 98% of RPO represented cloud-native subscriptions with non-cancelable terms greater than one year.
[Inference] Rising cloud subscription revenue plus RPO growth suggests customers are committing to multi-year cloud deployments rather than only short-cycle project work.
[Inference] Omnichannel retail complexity increases the value of integrated order, inventory, warehouse, transportation, labor, and store-execution systems.
[Hypothesis] Manhattan may capture some economics from supplier and partner connectivity through integrations, but direct EDI/trading-network monetization is not established by the current evidence.

[Comparative context from external search evidence] Consumer companies such as Samsonite and Designer Brands continue to emphasize DTC, ecommerce, retail stores, inventory management, sourcing, channel profitability, and omnichannel infrastructure, supporting the broader demand backdrop for retail execution systems; however, these are not direct evidence of Manhattan customer wins.
falsification_plan: Downgrade the thesis if future filings show cloud subscription revenue growth slowing sharply at the same time RPO growth weakens.
Downgrade if retail, omnichannel, store-fulfillment, or order-management exposure proves immaterial relative to broader WMS or non-retail supply-chain deployments.
Downgrade if services revenue weakness or commentary indicates implementation bottlenecks, delayed go-lives, or lower customer demand rather than a normal SaaS mix shift.
Downgrade if customer references show Manhattan is used mainly as a point WMS tool, not as a cross-channel system coordinating orders, inventory, stores, warehouses, transportation, and labor.

Falsify the supplier-network sub-thesis if evidence shows EDI/trading-partner connectivity is monetized mainly by separate B2B network vendors and Manhattan captures little recurring economics from those flows.
Downgrade if retailers increasingly choose competing OMS/WMS/TMS/POS platforms, ERP suites, or internally built systems for order orchestration and store fulfillment.
Downgrade if large customer concentration, project cancellations, or contract-duration changes weaken the durability implied by RPO.
deep_reports.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify whether Manhattan's retail and omnichannel exposure is large enough to make it a direct consumer-operating-workflow beneficiary, and separately verify whether it captures supplier-connectivity economics directly or only benefits indirectly through retail execution integrations. The hidden signal would be evidence that customers are standardizing Manhattan as the cross-channel system of record for inventory, order promising, store fulfillment, and warehouse/transportation execution rather than using it as a narrower WMS module.
next_research_tasks: Pull and parse Manhattan's full 2025 Form 10-K and latest 10-Q to verify cloud subscription revenue, RPO, RPO duration, revenue mix, customer concentration, and product language.
Build a product-by-workflow map: OMS, WMS, TMS, POS/store operations, labor management, inventory optimization, and integration/network capabilities.
Search customer case studies and implementation partner materials for evidence of retail order orchestration, ship-from-store, BOPIS, inventory availability, and unified commerce use cases.
Quantify vertical exposure: retail versus manufacturing, wholesale, logistics, grocery, apparel, consumer goods, and non-consumer supply-chain deployments.
Compare Manhattan against reference competitors in WMS, OMS, TMS, ecommerce, ERP, store systems, and EDI/B2B connectivity to identify where value accrues.
Specifically test the EDI/supplier-connectivity question: identify whether Manhattan owns recurring transaction/network revenue or primarily depends on integrations with third-party networks.

Use the two-lane Serenity funnel in the next layer: keep MANH as a reference benchmark while searching for underfollowed USD 300M-10B public companies in EDI/B2B networks, retail integration middleware, inventory data quality, returns logistics software, store execution, testing/compliance, and distributor workflow niches.
risks: Retail exposure may be smaller or less pure than assumed if growth is driven more by general warehouse, supply-chain, or non-retail deployments.
Cloud growth could decelerate if customers delay enterprise software migrations, reduce implementation budgets, or extend project timelines.
RPO growth may not translate cleanly into revenue acceleration if implementation capacity, customer go-lives, or services bottlenecks slow recognition.

Competitive pressure from ERP suites, ecommerce platforms, WMS/OMS specialists, TMS vendors, internal retailer systems, and emerging AI-native workflow tools could reduce Manhattan's strategic control.
Supplier-connectivity economics may accrue to EDI/B2B networks, integration platforms, marketplaces, ERPs, or retailer-owned data hubs rather than to Manhattan.
High-quality reference leaders can already be well understood by the market; multiple/valuation risk may be meaningful even if the operating thesis is correct.
Consumer weakness, discretionary retail pressure, tariffs, sourcing volatility, or inventory destocking could reduce retailers' appetite for large transformation projects.
deep_reports.supply_chain_position: Consumer demand layer -> retailers and brands -> omnichannel commerce / order management -> warehouse management -> transportation management -> store operations / POS -> labor management -> inventory optimization -> integrations with ERP, ecommerce platforms, carriers, suppliers, 3PLs, and marketplaces. Manhattan sits mainly in the retail execution and supply-chain software layer, not in physical retail goods, logistics assets, or consumer-facing marketplaces. It is a reference leader for software that coordinates fulfillment complexity after demand is generated.
deep_reports.thesis_cn: 【推论】Manhattan Associates 可能是消费零售全渠道执行层的关键系统供应商，因为大型零售商要同时协调线上订单、门店履约、仓库库存、运输路径、劳动力、POS/门店操作和库存优化。若消费者继续要求更快、更灵活的交付、退货、门店自提和跨渠道库存可见性，零售商会更依赖云原生 OMS/WMS/TMS/门店执行软件，把 Manhattan 推向核心运营系统层。根据已提供的 2025 10-K 摘要，Manhattan 2025 年云订阅收入为 4.081 亿美元，同比增长 21%，约占总收入 38%；RPO 约 22 亿美元，同比增长 25%，且超过 98% 的 RPO 来自期限超过一年的 cloud-native subscriptions。这说明云化需求和长期合同可见度较强。但它是否直接捕获供应商 EDI、交易伙伴网络或 B2B 连接网络经济，当前证据不足，应暂列为待验证假设。
deep_reports.thesis_en: [Inference] Manhattan Associates may be a consumer-retail operating-system chokepoint because large retailers must coordinate online orders, store fulfillment, warehouse inventory, transportation, labor, POS/store workflows, and inventory optimization across complex omnichannel networks. If consumers continue to demand faster delivery, flexible returns, BOPIS, ship-from-store, and real-time inventory visibility, retailers may rely more heavily on cloud-native OMS/WMS/TMS/store-execution platforms, pushing Manhattan closer to the operational core. Based on the provided 2025 10-K summary, Manhattan reported $408.1M of cloud subscription revenue in 2025, up 21% year over year and about 38% of total revenue; RPO was about $2.2B, up 25%, with more than 98% of RPO tied to cloud-native subscriptions with non-cancelable terms greater than one year. This supports durable cloud execution demand and contract visibility. However, direct capture of supplier EDI, trading-partner-network, or B2B connectivity economics is not yet proven and should remain a hypothesis.
deep_reports.title_cn: Manhattan Associates：零售全渠道履约操作系统的参考龙头，而非最隐蔽的供应链网络标的
deep_reports.title_en: Manhattan Associates: Reference Leader for Omnichannel Retail Execution, Not the Most Hidden Supplier-Network Chokepoint
deep_reports.why_underfollowed: Not truly underfollowed. Manhattan is a known vertical software compounder and therefore belongs in the reference lane, not the underfollowed alpha lane. The potentially missed angle is narrower: some investors may still frame it mainly as WMS software, while its strategic exposure extends into omnichannel order orchestration, store fulfillment, POS/store workflows, inventory optimization, transportation, and cloud-native retail execution. However, the company is much better known than obscure supplier-connectivity, EDI, testing, compliance, distributor, or niche workflow names, so it should not crowd out smaller hidden beneficiaries in later Serenity layers.

summary: Split Layer 5 deep reports generated one target at a time.
